blocks.text: Optical isomers are non-superimposable mirror images of each other. Optical isomerism is commonly shown by octahedral complexes with bidentate ligands, for example the nickel(II) complex of 1,2-diaminoethane (NH2CH2CH2NH2), [Ni(en)3]2+. Its two forms are mirror images that cannot be superimposed; such a pair is called enantiomers.

blocks.alt: Two octahedral sketches of [Ni(en)3]2+ on either side of a dashed mirror line. In each, the Ni ion is bonded to six N atoms and three curved purple links (en) each join two neighbouring N atoms. The right-hand form is the mirror image of the left.
blocks.caption: The two non-superimposable optical isomers of [Ni(en)3]2+ (original diagram after Figure 18.13).
blocks.long_description: Each 1,2-diaminoethane (en) ligand binds through two neighbouring positions, so three of them wrap round the nickel ion like the blades of a propeller. The two forms are mirror images of each other and cannot be superimposed, however they are turned: they are enantiomers, and they rotate plane-polarised light in opposite directions.

blocks.text: Optical isomers rotate the plane of polarised light in opposite directions. The isomer that rotates it to the right is dextrorotatory (+); the one that rotates it to the left is laevorotatory (-).

blocks.prompt: What type of ligand is most often needed for a complex to show optical isomerism?
blocks.explanation: A bidentate ligand (such as en) in an octahedral complex.

blocks.prompt: For [Ni(en)3]2+, state the coordination number and the type of ligand.
blocks.explanation: Coordination number 6 (three en, each forming two bonds); en is bidentate.

blocks.prompt: What isomerism does [Ni(NH2CH2CH2NH2)3]2+ show, and how do the isomers act on plane-polarised light?
blocks.explanation: Optical isomerism; the two enantiomers rotate the plane of polarised light by the same amount in opposite directions, one (+) to the right and the other (-) to the left.

blocks.prompt: Define optical isomers (enantiomers) in terms of mirror images and superimposability.
blocks.explanation: They are mirror images of each other that cannot be superimposed.

items: Typical of octahedral complexes with bidentate ligands, e.g. [Ni(en)3]2+.
